(iv) 'Fine-tuning and few-shot were both shown to sometimes worsen accuracy and calibration (e.g. gpt4o APT-extraction P/R 0.87->0.68 after fine-tuning; CVE-generation ECE 0.15->0.91) rather than merely partially improving as the abstract states -- is this degradation specific to small fine-tuning dataset size / overfitting, or a more general risk for CTI fine-tuning regardless of data volume?'

WHAT COUNTS AS A QUALIFYING SOURCE. The target is any INDEPENDENT study (different team from src-0001's) that MEASURES one or more of: repeated-query consistency / self-consistency / output stability across re-prompts or paraphrases; confidence calibration via ECE, Brier score, reliability diagrams, or verbalised-confidence-vs-accuracy comparison; abstention or selective-prediction behaviour; or uncertainty quantification -- applied to LLMs on CTI or security tasks. A source measuring calibration on security tasks generally (vulnerability detection, malware classification, security QA, SOC triage) is worth adding even if it is not narrowly CTI, PROVIDED you record the scope gap explicitly in the src file's limitations, exactly as src-0008 does. A source measuring calibration on general-domain tasks with no security content is NOT worth adding -- that literature is enormous and would flood the base with off-topic material; note it in the log and move on.

SEARCH DIRECTIONS, ordered by expected value. (1) Forward citations of src-0001 (arXiv 2503.23175, 'Large Language Models Are Unreliable for Cyber Threat Intelligence'): a paper citing it is the likeliest place to find a replication or extension. Note that semanticscholar.org/arxiv/<id> has returned 404 in this loop before (carry-forward [6]) -- try Google Scholar, the arXiv listing page, Connected Papers, or a plain web search on the exact title plus the word 'calibration'. (2) Direct searches: 'LLM calibration cybersecurity', 'expected calibration error security LLM benchmark', 'self-consistency LLM threat intelligence', 'uncertainty quantification LLM vulnerability detection', 'LLM overconfidence security tasks', 'verbalized confidence LLM security'. (3) Check whether CTIBench (src-0002), CyberSOCEval (src-0005) or CyberThreat-Eval (src-0007) have LATER versions, companion papers, or leaderboard extensions that added a consistency or calibration axis -- open_question (ii) and (iii) are specifically about whether the finding replicates on THOSE model lists and THOSE sub-tasks, so an updated version of one of those benchmarks would be the single highest-value find available. (4) Security-conference proceedings 2025-2026 (NDSS, CCS, USENIX Security, S&P) and arXiv cs.CR listings for calibration/uncertainty papers.

If you find a source that makes the abstention-vs-hallucination link on CTI material, that lead becomes attachable and is worth saying so.
